reply_text:
I'm building the "show movement" chart: how many rows each shared stop blocks, over time. Then I'll send out the next-stop discovery jobs.Rendering the new chart to check its layout, then I'll send out the discovery jobs.Chart's live. Now the next-stop discovery.㊥ (show movement, find next steps) Both are under way. The progress page has a new chart showing how many rows each shared stop blocks over time, and two seats are now finding the stops that come after the current ones.

㊢ (the movement chart) It's at https://zone.hyperreal.enterprises/wip/mfuton-progress.html, and I checked a rendered screenshot. It shows the pattern I described earlier. "Source projection" climbed to 43 rows during the afternoon, then fell to 4 when the `term[_]` merge landed. In the same step, "`term[_]` quotation coercion" jumped from 2 to 38. Right now the stops are:

| shared stop | rows |
|---|---|
| `term[_]` quotation coercion | 38 |
| other, mostly not re-probed recently | 33 |
| metavariable postponed | 9 |
| `null.<field>` receiver | 5 |
| source projection | 4 |

The 15-minute update loop now refreshes this chart too. One caveat: points before the live snapshots are reconstructed from the commit time of the code that was probed, which can be earlier than the probe itself. The page says so.

㊢ (finding the next stops)
- **codex-6** is re-probing the 45 rows that haven't been probed since the `term[_]` merge. It runs 4 lanes, warm, which is fine for discovery, and groups the rows by their current stop.
- **codex-25** is finding what the `term[_]`-blocked rows hit after that stop, before the real fix lands. It uses codex-18's rejected shortcut, which gives the type Lean uses for these rows' case, applied only in its own worktrees. Those results are recorded under a commit name that isn't on cand-1, so they can't count towards the curve.
- **claude-3** is tracing the `null.<field>` stop (5 rows that never reach `term[_]`) in Lean. That becomes a packet for another idle seat.

Each group table becomes a Lean-traced discovery, then one fix packet per group. So when codex-18's fix lands, the next fixes should already be in progress rather than waiting to be found.

㊣ (Rob's main) Understood. The dropped work is restored: codex-4 classified every change of Rob's that the merge dropped. The 6 that mattered are back in `d6b0b096`, including the three definitions his code calls, which had stopped the merge from loading. The other 12 are recorded with the cand-1 commit that covers each one, or the reason for our choice. The five-row cold check is the last gate. If it passes, I'll check the merge in to Rob's main and report the commit.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (the flat loss at 90) The loss has been flat at 90 since 17:38 because every remaining row is stuck behind the same one or two shared defects, and the loss only counts rows that reach the end. We cleared the first shared defect, which affected 43 rows, at about 18:20. Within minutes nearly the same rows hit the next one: the `term[_]` coercion, 36 of the 44 re-probed rows plus `atEnd` and `mkUnexpectedError`. Fixes have been moving rows to later stops, but none has reached correct yet.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(why it isn't rapid) There are three reasons:
- **The work queues behind one defect.** The `term[_]` list-literal macro is in the dependencies of almost every remaining row. Until that one fix lands, more seats on other rows can't be tested, because they stop at `term[_]` first.
- **Each remaining row probably has several stops in series.** Each stop costs a discovery, a fix and a cold acceptance of about 30 minutes. Warm runs sped up discovery (claude-3's 44-row re-probe took about 65 minutes instead of 2.5 hours), but acceptance stays cold by design.
- **I spent effort on things that don't move the curve by design.** The comparison with Rob's main and the merge took most of codex-4's afternoon and much of my review. It turned up a real regression on his side and a merge that dropped his code, but it moved no rows.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (where it stands) codex-18 is on the `term[_]` fix, working from claude-3's Lean trace. codex-19 independently found the same root cause, so I'm fairly confident about the diagnosis. Its test needed one correction: it failed for a reason that wouldn't prove anything. My rough estimate for the fix plus cold acceptance is 1.5 to 2 hours. When it lands, many rows will move at once, but to their next stops, not necessarily to correct. The loss should start falling after that, in steps rather than smoothly.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what I'd change) Two changes:
1. **Show movement before rows finish.** Add a second curve to the progress page: rows blocked by each shared stop over time (43 → 0 for source projection, 36 → ? for `term[_]`). That shows whether the work is moving, and you can see a chokepoint as it forms.
2. **Find the next stops in advance.** We have the Lean elaborator census, which lists each row's features that no correct row has used yet. While codex-18 works, I can give the idle seats (codex-25, codex-6, and codex-24 once its controls finish) discovery only, Lean-traced, on the next most common of those features. Then the fixes are ready when `term[_]` clears, and we don't find each stop one at a time.
